hints: Focus on what structure actually gives that yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine, the triiodomethane or iodoform test.
Recall that ethanal, methyl ketones and alcohols containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group are positive, then work out the organic product in each reaction.
Check which product contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ unit that can be cleaved to $\text{CHI}_3$, and eliminate oxidised acids and primary alcohols.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform test**

Yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(\text{aq})$ means triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, has formed. This is positive only for a few groups.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO, CH}_3\text{CO-R and CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-R give CHI}_3$$

**Work out the product of each reaction**

Think hydrolysis, oxidation and reduction separately. Do not confuse the starting material with the product tested.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \text{Cl}^-$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Match products to the iodoform rule**

Only propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit. It is oxidised in situ and then cleaved to give yellow $\text{CHI}_3$.

Positive result:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{CHI}_3(s, yellow) + \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$$

options.A: Warming 2-chloropropane with aqueous NaOH gives nucleophilic substitution to propan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH3. This is a secondary alcohol with the CH3CH(OH)- group, so it gives a positive iodoform test and yellow CHI3 precipitate.
options.B: Ethanal itself would be positive, but heating under reflux with acidified dichromate(VI) fully oxidises it to ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. Carboxylic acids do not give the iodoform reaction, so no yellow precipitate forms.
options.C: Acid hydrolysis of methyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid plus methanol. Neither CH3COOH nor CH3OH contains CH3CO- or CH3CH(OH)-, so neither gives CHI3. Students who spot CH3 in the ester often wrongly assume it is a methyl ketone.
options.D: NaBH4 reduces propanal to the primary alcohol propan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2OH. This lacks the CH3CH(OH)- grouping (the OH is on a CH2, not on a carbon bearing a CH3), so it is iodoform negative.
